# zdscal

> Scale a complex double-precision vector by a double-precision constant.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zdscal from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/zdscal';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zdscal( N, alpha, x, strideX ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `alpha` | `number` | Real scalar multiplier |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `zx` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `alpha`: On entry, `DA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: output array

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zdscal.strided( N, alpha, x, strideX, offsetX ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `alpha` | `number` | Real scalar multiplier |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `zx` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `zx` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `alpha`: On entry, `DA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `zx`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zdscal()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZDSCAL`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zdscal.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zdscal from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/zdscal';

// Scale a complex vector by a real constant:
const zx = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
zdscal( 2, 2.0, zx, 1 );
console.log( reinterpret( zx, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
zdscal.strided( 2, 2.0, zx, 1, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( zx, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZDSCAL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZDSCAL scales a vector by a constant.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, 3/11/78. modified 3/93 to return if incx .le. 0. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
